meta.title: ContextWatchdog — redact in place before you paste, without your data leaving the machine
meta.description: An open-source, free, serverless browser extension. It detects and replaces secrets and personal data before you send text to an AI — entirely on your own device.

hero.badge: Open source · Free · No server · No account
hero.title: Redact in place, before you paste
hero.subtitle: Before you paste a config, a log, a ticket or a stack trace into an AI, ContextWatchdog finds the secrets and personal data inside it and replaces them with placeholders in place. Detection and replacement happen entirely on your device — the text never leaves it.

demo.title: 30 seconds
demo.caption: Paste a config containing a database password: the original text is inserted normally first (input is never blocked), then replaced **in place** with placeholders once detection finishes, with a brief "3 redactions" toast in the corner. Nothing interrupts what you were doing.
demo.placeholderNote: Placeholders stay semantic, so the redacted config is still understandable to the AI.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Two detection tiers — one always on, one optional — sharing a single dedupe and arbitration pass.

steps.title: Regex tier (always on)
steps.body: Targets with a fixed shape — secrets, connection strings, phone numbers, national IDs, bank cards, email, IPs, plates — are matched by regex plus algorithmic validation: ISO 7064 for Chinese ID numbers, Luhn for bank cards, mod-97 for IBANs, area-segment rules for US SSNs. Zero latency, works offline.

steps.title: AI tier (optional)
steps.body: Entities with no fixed shape — names, addresses — go to a local GLiNER model (WASM). It only sees the spans the regex tier did not already cover, and it must be explicitly enabled and downloaded by you (a quantised model, ~180 MB, once). If the model is unavailable the pipeline degrades to pure regex: no errors, no blocking.

steps.title: Placeholder sharing
steps.body: A value appearing N times becomes the same placeholder everywhere; overlapping spans are merged by type priority (secrets > personal data > high entropy), so replacements never cut into each other. Placeholders stay semantic, so the redacted text remains readable and inferable for the AI.

privacy.title: Verifiable privacy claims
privacy.lead: Every row below can be checked in this repository — you do not have to take our word for it.

items.claim: The extension never sends your text to a server
items.how: Exactly two fetch calls exist in the repository, both in modelDownload.ts, both used only to download the model. No XHR, sendBeacon or WebSocket anywhere.

items.claim: The only network activity is the model download, and only if you enable it
items.how: The AI tier is off by default. Once you enable it, model files are fetched from whitelisted sources (a ModelScope mirror, falling back to huggingface.co).
The manifest declares no content_scripts and does not request <all_urls>, only optional_host_permissions. The paste listener is injected only after your approval.

items.claim: No telemetry, no analytics, no crash reporting
items.how: There is no analytics or reporting SDK in the repository. Run npm run build yourself and inspect the bundle for suspicious requests or remote domains.
type=password inputs and hidden fields are skipped at isTextEditable, and that guard sits on both the paste-injection and the side-panel paths, with no exceptions.
Every Release ships sha256 checksums, and LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt travel with the bundle, so any change to the source code alters them.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.lead: Not promises — the actual numbers in this repository today.

thanks.title: Thank-you wall
thanks.lead: Donations buy time, not features. Every feature is free.

items.q: Does it upload my text anywhere?
items.a: No. Detection and replacement run entirely on your device (service worker or side-panel memory). The only network activity in the whole repository is downloading model files, and only after you enable the AI tier yourself.

items.q: Do I have to download the AI model?
items.a: No. The regex tier is always on and covers secrets, connection strings, phone numbers, national IDs, bank cards, IBANs and other fixed-shape targets — zero latency, offline. The AI tier only adds shapeless entities like names and addresses. The quantised model is about 180 MB, downloaded once and then served from the browser cache; if it is unavailable the pipeline falls back to pure regex.

items.q: What if it flags something that is not sensitive?
items.a: Switch that row from "replace" to "keep" and it stays as-is for this run. If the same type keeps false-positiving, create a custom profile to change that type's default action, or add the value to the whitelist. Issues are welcome too — false positives are the most important problem for a tool like this.

items.q: Which sites does it work on?
items.a: The side panel does not depend on any site and always works. Paste interception requires per-site authorisation: you add a domain, the browser asks you to grant access, and only then is the listener injected. Unauthorised sites are completely untouched, and the manifest contains no content_scripts or all_urls.

items.q: Does it support rich-text editors in web pages?
items.a: Currently input[type=text/search] and textarea. contenteditable rich-text areas are not handled — paste fragments are hard to locate reliably there, and it is better to skip them than to ship a version that occasionally rewrites the wrong part.

items.q: Which interface languages are available? Do placeholders follow?
items.a: Chinese and English for now. The interface language also decides the placeholder wording: a Chinese UI produces <<手机号>>, an English UI produces <<PHONE>>. The parser accepts names from both languages, so mapping tables written before a language switch still restore correctly.

Yes — Apache-2.0 permits closed-source commercial use. The conditions are that you keep the copyright and NOTICE notices, mark your changes, and use your own name and icons; the ContextWatchdog name and icon are the author's trademark and are not covered by the code licence.

items.q: Will there be paid features later?
items.a: No. Every feature is fully enabled right now: no paid tier, no quota, no accounts. Donations cover maintenance time and unlock nothing — the extension's own capability panel says the same thing.

donate.title: Support the project
donate.lead: The project is free, serverless and account-free, so it earns nothing to cover the time it takes to maintain. If it ever saved you from one incident, you can buy me a coffee.
donate.body: Donating unlocks nothing — there is nothing locked. The supporter list and the payment code are maintained locally, with no third-party analytics involved.

footer.static: This site is static: no client-side scripts (bar one copy button), no CDN, no third-party analytics, no web fonts.

privacyPage.title: Privacy policy
privacyPage.lead: In one sentence: we do not collect any of your data. The verifiable details are below.
privacyPage.noCollect: ContextWatchdog does not collect, upload or store any of your text or personal information. No account, no telemetry, no third-party analytics SDK.

flowRows.where: on-device (service worker or side-panel memory); never leaves your machine
on-device (WASM / ONNX Runtime); never leaves your machine
whitelisted model sources (a ModelScope mirror, falling back to huggingface.co); model files only — user data is never uploaded
per-site, stored in chrome.storage.local; unauthorised sites are never touched

privacyPage.thirdParty: The third-party components in use and their licences are listed in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (both inside the bundle and in the repository). The model downloaded at runtime is onnx-community/gliner_small-v2 (Apache-2.0).
privacyPage.contact: Open an issue for anything privacy-related.
